summary: A brick tower on Naval Air Station Pensacola, lit in 1859 to replace an 1824 tower, shelled in 1861, and still showing its first-order Fresnel lens.

The record's 1858 and 1859 are the second tower's completion (1858) and lighting (1 Jan 1859).

notes_for_editor: Narrative for 1824-1886 and 2006-2018 rests mainly on the Pensacola Lighthouse Association page and LighthouseFriends, whose texts are near-identical (one lineage, not two independent sources). Disagreements: contract date for first tower (2 Apr per association/LF vs 13 Apr 1824 per NRHP); tower height (160 ft NRHP, 159 ft association, 150 ft elsewhere); Civil War damage (NRHP says light put out of order; association says tower in good condition); date of black-and-white daymark (association: 1869; NRHP: drawing c. 1877 shows it); relighting after the war (association: fourth-order lens 20 Dec 1862; Wikipedia says 1863; NRHP says restored 1869); Michaela Ingraham's end year (1854 roster, 1855 association/LF); dwelling year (1868 USLHS, 1869 association). The NRHP OCR is poor ('11*23', '18^9', '185-4'); figures read from it were matched against the other sources. NRHP entry year taken from the OCR'd stamp 'JUL 1519T4' (15 July 1974 per other listings). The 1919 Thompson/Purcell quarrel and the 1936 Eastern Airlines landing rest on LighthouseFriends only. The 1917 Bulletin commendation covers a district-wide group of 20 employees; its description of their work is general, not specific to Pensacola. Light characteristic left out: record says F G, other sources differ. The Bulletin pages were matched by the corpus tool's PDF page numbers; the printed page for the 1917 commendation is 297. Newspaper searches (Chronicling America, Florida papers 1880-1917) found nothing relevant. Keeper roster lines all come from the USLHS archive page (assistant-keeper columns 'Thomas Clairmon Brooks' appears twice; David R. Hurd has no end year).
